title: Relative clauses advanced
note: whose and whom · preposition + which/whom, fronted and stranded · non-defining clauses with commas, which for a whole clause, quantifier + of which/whom · reduced relatives (-ing active, -ed passive) · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-06 (cloud run 7)

items.en: I met a woman whose brother is a doctor.
items.cz: Potkal jsem ženu, jejíž bratr je doktor.
items.gap: I met a woman ____ brother is a doctor.
accepts: I met a woman whose brother is a doctor.
items.explanation: whose = possession. A noun follows it directly, with no article.
items.explanation_cz: whose = přivlastnění. Hned za ním stojí podstatné jméno, bez členu.

items.en: This is the house whose roof was repaired.
items.cz: Tohle je dům, jehož střecha byla opravena.
items.gap: This is the house ____ roof was repaired.
accepts: This is the house whose roof was repaired.
items.explanation: whose works for things too, not only people.
items.explanation_cz: whose se používá i pro věci, nejen pro osoby.

items.en: The colleague whose laptop was stolen works with me.
items.cz: Kolega, kterému ukradli notebook, pracuje se mnou.
items.gap: The colleague ____ laptop was stolen works with me.
accepts: The colleague whose laptop was stolen works with me.
items.explanation: Czech says komu; English needs whose in front of the thing owned.
items.explanation_cz: Čeština řekne "komu"; angličtina potřebuje whose před vlastněnou věcí.

items.en: She has a friend whose sister works in a hotel.
items.cz: Má kamarádku, jejíž sestra pracuje v hotelu.
items.gap: She has a friend ____ sister works in a hotel.
accepts: She has a friend whose sister works in a hotel.
items.explanation: whose is one word and never has an apostrophe. who's = who is.
items.explanation_cz: whose je jedno slovo a nikdy nemá apostrof. who's = who is.

items.en: The company whose price was best signed the contract.
items.cz: Firma, jejíž cena byla nejlepší, podepsala tu smlouvu.
items.gap: The company ____ price was best signed the contract.
accepts: The company whose price was best signed the contract.
items.explanation: whose + noun is much lighter than the formal of which.
items.explanation_cz: whose + podstatné jméno je mnohem lehčí než formální of which.

items.en: He is the teacher whose students always pass.
items.cz: To je ten učitel, jehož studenti vždycky projdou.
items.gap: He is the teacher ____ students always pass.
accepts: He is the teacher whose students always pass.
items.explanation: whose + noun, then the clause carries on normally.
items.explanation_cz: whose + podstatné jméno, a věta pokračuje běžným způsobem.

items.en: The man whom we met yesterday is her boss.
items.cz: Muž, kterého jsme včera potkali, je její šéf.
items.gap: The man ____ we met yesterday is her boss.
accepts: The man whom we met yesterday is her boss.
The man who we met yesterday is her boss.
The man we met yesterday is her boss.
items.explanation: whom is the object of met. In speech who or nothing is normal.
items.explanation_cz: whom je předmět slovesa met. V mluvené řeči se běžně říká who nebo nic.

items.en: The client whom I called was very busy.
items.cz: Klient, kterému jsem volal, měl hodně práce.
items.gap: The client ____ I called was very busy.
accepts: The client whom I called was very busy.
The client who I called was very busy.
The client I called was very busy.
items.explanation: A subject (I) follows, so the relative word is the object: whom.
items.explanation_cz: Následuje podmět (I), takže vztažné slovo je předmět: whom.

items.en: The students whom she taught still write to her.
items.cz: Studenti, které učila, jí pořád píšou.
items.gap: The students ____ she taught still write to her.
accepts: The students whom she taught still write to her.
The students who she taught still write to her.
items.explanation: whom for people as object; which would be wrong here.
items.explanation_cz: whom pro osoby v předmětu; which by tu bylo špatně.

items.en: The woman whom you invited has arrived.
items.cz: Žena, kterou jsi pozval, dorazila.
items.gap: The woman ____ you invited has arrived.
accepts: The woman whom you invited has arrived.
The woman who you invited has arrived.
items.explanation: Test: if you could answer him or her, use whom.
items.explanation_cz: Test: pokud byste odpověděli him nebo her, patří tam whom.

items.en: The hotel whose garden we saw is very old.
items.cz: Hotel, jehož zahradu jsme viděli, je velmi starý.
items.gap: The hotel ____ garden we saw is very old.
accepts: The hotel whose garden we saw is very old.
items.explanation: The garden belongs to the hotel, so whose — even for a building.
items.explanation_cz: Zahrada patří hotelu, takže whose — i u budovy.

items.en: The people whom we invited did not come.
items.cz: Lidé, které jsme pozvali, nepřišli.
items.gap: The people ____ we invited did not come.
accepts: The people whom we invited did not come.
The people who we invited did not come.
The people we invited did not come.
items.explanation: Object again — and here you can drop the relative word completely.
items.explanation_cz: Opět předmět — a tady lze vztažné slovo úplně vynechat.

items.en: The people with whom I work are friendly.
items.cz: Lidé, se kterými pracuji, jsou přátelští.
items.gap: The people with ____ I work are friendly.
accepts: The people with whom I work are friendly.
The people I work with are friendly.
items.explanation: After a preposition it must be whom, never who or that.
items.explanation_cz: Po předložce musí být whom, nikdy who ani that.

items.en: This is the hotel in which we stayed last year.
items.cz: Tohle je hotel, ve kterém jsme loni bydleli.
items.gap: This is the hotel in ____ we stayed last year.
accepts: This is the hotel in which we stayed last year.
This is the hotel we stayed in last year.
This is the hotel in which we lived last year.
This is the hotel we lived in last year.
items.explanation: After a preposition it must be which for things — never that.
items.explanation_cz: Po předložce musí být u věcí which — nikdy that.

items.en: The manager to whom I sent the report is away.
items.cz: Manažer, kterému jsem poslal tu zprávu, je pryč.
items.gap: The manager to ____ I sent the report is away.
accepts: The manager to whom I sent the report is away.
The manager I sent the report to is away.
items.explanation: Fronted preposition + whom is the formal, written option.
items.explanation_cz: Předložka vpředu + whom je formální, psaná varianta.

items.en: The flat in which they live is very small.
items.cz: Byt, ve kterém bydlí, je velmi malý.
items.gap: The flat in ____ they live is very small.
accepts: The flat in which they live is very small.
The flat they live in is very small.
items.explanation: in which = where. Both are correct here.
items.explanation_cz: in which = where. Obojí je tu správně.

items.en: That is the box I was looking for.
items.cz: To je ta krabice, kterou jsem hledal.
items.gap: That is the box I was looking ____.
accepts: That is the box I was looking for.
That is the box for which I was looking.
items.explanation: In speech the preposition stays at the end and the relative word disappears.
items.explanation_cz: V mluvené řeči zůstává předložka na konci a vztažné slovo zmizí.

items.en: The hotel which we stayed in was cheap.
items.cz: Hotel, ve kterém jsme bydleli, byl levný.
items.gap: The hotel which we stayed ____ was cheap.
accepts: The hotel which we stayed in was cheap.
The hotel we stayed in was cheap.
The hotel which we lived in was cheap.
The hotel we lived in was cheap.
items.explanation: Same sentence as in which, only relaxed: the preposition drops to the end.
items.explanation_cz: Stejná věta jako s in which, jen uvolněná: předložka spadne na konec.

items.en: The manager whom I work for is in Prague today.
items.cz: Manažer, pro kterého pracuji, je dnes v Praze.
items.gap: The manager whom I work ____ is in Prague today.
accepts: The manager whom I work for is in Prague today.
The manager I work for is in Prague today.
items.explanation: work for somebody — the preposition belongs to the verb, so learn them together.
items.explanation_cz: work for somebody — předložka patří ke slovesu, učte se je společně.

items.en: This is the shop from which I bought the laptop.
items.cz: Tohle je obchod, ve kterém jsem koupil ten notebook.
items.gap: This is the shop from ____ I bought the laptop.
accepts: This is the shop from which I bought the laptop.
This is the shop I bought the laptop from.
items.explanation: from which for things; that can never follow a preposition.
items.explanation_cz: from which pro věci; that nemůže nikdy stát po předložce.

items.en: The friend with whom I studied is a teacher.
items.cz: Kamarád, se kterým jsem studoval, je učitel.
items.gap: The friend with ____ I studied is a teacher.
accepts: The friend with whom I studied is a teacher.
The friend I studied with is a teacher.
items.explanation: with whom, never with who.
items.explanation_cz: with whom, nikdy with who.

items.en: The project which she is working on is very big.
items.cz: Projekt, na kterém pracuje, je velmi velký.
items.gap: The project which she is working ____ is very big.
accepts: The project which she is working on is very big.
The project she is working on is very big.
items.explanation: work on a project — the preposition stays with the verb at the end.
items.explanation_cz: work on a project — předložka zůstává se slovesem na konci.

items.en: The room in which we had the meeting is small.
items.cz: Místnost, ve které jsme měli tu schůzku, je malá.
items.gap: The room in ____ we had the meeting is small.
accepts: The room in which we had the meeting is small.
The room where we had the meeting is small.
items.explanation: For a place, in which and where do the same job.
items.explanation_cz: U místa dělají in which a where totéž.

items.en: The woman to whom you spoke is my sister.
items.cz: Žena, se kterou jsi mluvil, je moje sestra.
items.gap: The woman to ____ you spoke is my sister.
accepts: The woman to whom you spoke is my sister.
The woman you spoke to is my sister.
items.explanation: speak TO somebody — English keeps the preposition even when Czech uses a case.
items.explanation_cz: speak TO somebody — angličtina drží předložku i tam, kde čeština použije pád.

items.en: My boss, who lives in Brno, is on holiday.
items.cz: Můj šéf, který bydlí v Brně, je na dovolené.
items.gap: My boss, ____ lives in Brno, is on holiday.
accepts: My boss, who lives in Brno, is on holiday.
items.explanation: Between commas the clause is extra information — and that is never allowed there.
items.explanation_cz: Mezi čárkami je věta doplňující informací — a that tam nikdy nesmí být.

items.en: Prague, which I visited last year, is very old.
items.cz: Praha, kterou jsem loni navštívil, je velmi stará.
items.gap: Prague, ____ I visited last year, is very old.
accepts: Prague, which I visited last year, is very old.
items.explanation: A name is already identified, so the clause can only be non-defining.
items.explanation_cz: Vlastní jméno je už určené, takže věta může být jen doplňující.

items.en: My sister, whose flat is in London, works in a bank.
items.cz: Moje sestra, jejíž byt je v Londýně, pracuje v bance.
items.gap: My sister, ____ flat is in London, works in a bank.
accepts: My sister, whose flat is in London, works in a bank.
items.explanation: whose works inside a non-defining clause too.
items.explanation_cz: whose funguje i uvnitř doplňující věty.

items.en: There are three reasons, two of which are important.
items.cz: Jsou tři důvody, z nichž dva jsou důležité.
items.gap: There are three reasons, two ____ which are important.
accepts: There are three reasons, two of which are important.
items.explanation: number or quantifier + of which for things.
items.explanation_cz: číslovka nebo kvantifikátor + of which u věcí.

items.en: We invited ten people, most of whom came.
items.cz: Pozvali jsme deset lidí, z nichž většina přišla.
items.gap: We invited ten people, most of ____ came.
accepts: We invited ten people, most of whom came.
items.explanation: of whom for people. Not of who and not of them.
items.explanation_cz: of whom u osob. Ne of who ani of them.

items.en: The office was closed, which was a problem.
items.cz: Kancelář byla zavřená, což byl problém.
items.gap: The office was closed, ____ was a problem.
accepts: The office was closed, which was a problem.
items.explanation: Here which stands for the whole first clause — Czech což.
items.explanation_cz: Zde which zastupuje celou první větu — česky "což".

items.en: She helped me with the report, which was very kind.
items.cz: Pomohla mi se zprávou, což bylo velmi milé.
items.gap: She helped me with the report, ____ was very kind.
accepts: She helped me with the report, which was very kind.
items.explanation: Comment on the whole sentence: comma + which, never what.
items.explanation_cz: Komentář k celé větě: čárka + which, nikdy what.

items.en: My neighbour, who has two dogs, is very nice.
items.cz: Můj soused, který má dva psy, je velmi milý.
items.gap: My neighbour, ____ has two dogs, is very nice.
accepts: My neighbour, who has two dogs, is very nice.
items.explanation: who is the subject of has, so whom would be wrong.
items.explanation_cz: who je podmět slovesa has, takže whom by bylo špatně.

items.en: The hotel, where we stayed last year, is now closed.
items.cz: Hotel, kde jsme loni bydleli, je teď zavřený.
items.gap: The hotel, ____ we stayed last year, is now closed.
accepts: The hotel, where we stayed last year, is now closed.
The hotel, where we lived last year, is now closed.
items.explanation: where for a place; no preposition is needed after it.
items.explanation_cz: where u místa; po něm už není třeba předložka.

items.en: I have two brothers, both of whom live in Prague.
items.cz: Mám dva bratry, kteří oba žijí v Praze.
items.gap: I have two brothers, both of ____ live in Prague.
accepts: I have two brothers, both of whom live in Prague.
items.explanation: both of whom — this pattern only works with a relative word, not them.
items.explanation_cz: both of whom — tato vazba funguje jen se vztažným slovem, ne s them.

items.en: The books, which I bought last week, are on the table.
items.cz: Ty knihy, které jsem koupil minulý týden, leží na stole.
items.gap: The books, ____ I bought last week, are on the table.
accepts: The books, which I bought last week, are on the table.
items.explanation: With commas you cannot use that, and you cannot leave the word out.
items.explanation_cz: S čárkami nelze použít that ani vztažné slovo vynechat.

items.en: The film, which was very long, was boring.
items.cz: Ten film, který byl velmi dlouhý, byl nudný.
items.gap: The film, ____ was very long, was boring.
accepts: The film, which was very long, was boring.
items.explanation: Take the clause out and the sentence still works — that is the test for commas.
items.explanation_cz: Vypusťte vedlejší větu a hlavní věta pořád funguje — to je test na čárky.

items.en: The man sitting by the window is my boss.
items.cz: Muž sedící u okna je můj šéf.
items.gap: The man ____ by the window is my boss.
accepts: The man sitting by the window is my boss.
The man who is sitting by the window is my boss.
items.explanation: who is sitting shortens to sitting. Active meaning, so -ing.
items.explanation_cz: who is sitting se zkracuje na sitting. Aktivní význam, proto -ing.

items.en: The book written by her sister is very good.
items.cz: Kniha, kterou napsala její sestra, je velmi dobrá.
items.gap: The book ____ by her sister is very good.
accepts: The book written by her sister is very good.
The book which was written by her sister is very good.
items.explanation: which was written shortens to written. Passive meaning, so the past participle.
items.explanation_cz: which was written se zkracuje na written. Pasivní význam, proto příčestí minulé.

items.en: The people waiting at the station are students.
items.cz: Lidé čekající na nádraží jsou studenti.
items.gap: The people ____ at the station are students.
accepts: The people waiting at the station are students.
The people who are waiting at the station are students.
items.explanation: They are doing the waiting, so -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Oni sami čekají, proto -ing.

items.en: The tools needed for the job are in the box.
items.cz: Nástroje potřebné k té práci jsou v krabici.
items.gap: The tools ____ for the job are in the box.
accepts: The tools needed for the job are in the box.
The tools which are needed for the job are in the box.
items.explanation: The tools are needed by somebody — passive, so -ed.
items.explanation_cz: Nástroje jsou někým potřeba — pasivum, proto -ed.

items.en: The people interested in the job should call us.
items.cz: Lidé, kteří mají zájem o tu práci, by nám měli zavolat.
items.gap: The people ____ in the job should call us.
accepts: The people interested in the job should call us.
The people who are interested in the job should call us.
items.explanation: People are interested; a job is interesting. The reduced clause keeps that difference.
items.explanation_cz: Lidé jsou interested; práce je interesting. Zkrácená věta ten rozdíl zachovává.

items.en: The letter sent last week has arrived.
items.cz: Dopis odeslaný minulý týden dorazil.
items.gap: The letter ____ last week has arrived.
accepts: The letter sent last week has arrived.
The letter which was sent last week has arrived.
items.explanation: Somebody sent the letter — passive, so the past participle.
items.explanation_cz: Dopis někdo odeslal — pasivum, proto příčestí minulé.

items.en: The woman standing at the door is my teacher.
items.cz: Žena stojící u dveří je moje učitelka.
items.gap: The woman ____ at the door is my teacher.
accepts: The woman standing at the door is my teacher.
The woman who is standing at the door is my teacher.
items.explanation: Active again: she is doing the standing.
items.explanation_cz: Opět aktivum: ona sama stojí.

items.en: The car stolen last week was found in Brno.
items.cz: Auto ukradené minulý týden se našlo v Brně.
items.gap: The car ____ last week was found in Brno.
accepts: The car stolen last week was found in Brno.
The car which was stolen last week was found in Brno.
items.explanation: Irregular past participle, same rule: passive means -ed or the third form.
items.explanation_cz: Nepravidelné příčestí, stejné pravidlo: pasivum znamená -ed nebo třetí tvar.

items.en: The students studying English need more time.
items.cz: Studenti studující angličtinu potřebují víc času.
items.gap: The students ____ English need more time.
accepts: The students studying English need more time.
The students who study English need more time.
items.explanation: The -ing form covers who study as well as who are studying.
items.explanation_cz: Tvar s -ing pokrývá jak who study, tak who are studying.

items.en: The report finished yesterday is on your table.
items.cz: Zpráva dokončená včera leží na tvém stole.
items.gap: The report ____ yesterday is on your table.
accepts: The report finished yesterday is on your table.
The report which was finished yesterday is on your table.
items.explanation: Passive: somebody finished it.
items.explanation_cz: Pasivum: někdo ji dokončil.

items.en: The people living in that house are very nice.
items.cz: Lidé žijící v tom domě jsou velmi milí.
items.gap: The people ____ in that house are very nice.
accepts: The people living in that house are very nice.
The people who live in that house are very nice.
items.explanation: who live shortens to living even though the full clause has no be.
items.explanation_cz: who live se zkracuje na living, i když plná věta žádné be nemá.

items.en: The books bought last month are still in the box.
items.cz: Knihy koupené minulý měsíc jsou pořád v krabici.
items.gap: The books ____ last month are still in the box.
accepts: The books bought last month are still in the box.
The books which were bought last month are still in the box.
items.explanation: Passive with an irregular participle: bought.
items.explanation_cz: Pasivum s nepravidelným příčestím: bought.

cards.title: whose and whom — the two words B1 skipped
cards.title_cz: whose a whom — dvě slova, která B1 přeskočilo
cards.body: **whose** says the thing belongs to somebody, and a noun follows it **directly** — no article, no apostrophe. **whom** is the object form of who: use it when a subject follows, and always after a preposition.
cards.body_cz: **whose** říká, že něco někomu patří, a hned za ním následuje podstatné jméno — bez členu, bez apostrofu. **whom** je předmětný tvar od who: použijte ho, když následuje podmět, a vždy po předložce.

table.caption: Which word, and why
rows: My boss, who lives in Brno, is on holiday.
The man whom we met is her boss.
I met a woman whose brother is a doctor.
The books, which I bought last week, are here.

cards.title: The preposition can go in front or at the end
cards.title_cz: Předložka může stát vpředu i na konci
cards.body: Both versions are correct; they differ in register. Front the preposition and you must use **whom** or **which** — *that* and *who* are impossible there. Leave it at the end and the relative word can disappear completely, which is what people actually say.
cards.body_cz: Obě varianty jsou správné; liší se stylem. Když dáte předložku dopředu, musíte použít **whom** nebo **which** — *that* ani *who* tam nemohou. Když ji necháte na konci, vztažné slovo může úplně zmizet — a přesně tak lidé mluví.
points: Formal: The manager to whom I sent the report is away.
Neutral: The manager who I sent the report to is away.
Spoken: The manager I sent the report to is away.
Never: the manager to who / the hotel in that

cards.title: Commas change the meaning, not just the punctuation
cards.body: Without commas the clause **identifies** which one you mean. With commas it only **adds** information you could delete. In the comma version **that is banned**, the relative word can **never** be left out, and **which** can point back at the whole sentence — the English for Czech *což*.
cards.body_cz: Bez čárek vedlejší věta **určuje**, o kterou věc jde. S čárkami jen **doplňuje** informaci, kterou byste mohli vypustit. Ve variantě s čárkami je **that zakázáno**, vztažné slovo **nelze** vynechat a **which** může odkazovat na celou větu — anglický protějšek českého "což".
points: The students who passed can go home. (only those students)
The students, who passed, can go home. (all of them, and they passed)
The office was closed, which was a problem. (which = the whole fact)
We invited ten people, most of whom came. (quantifier + of whom)

cards.title: Cutting the clause down: -ing or -ed
cards.body: Drop the relative word and the **be**, and a short participle phrase is left. The choice is only ever about direction: if the noun **does** the action you keep **-ing**; if the action is **done to** it you keep the **past participle**.
cards.body_cz: Vynechte vztažné slovo a sloveso **be** a zbude krátká participiální vazba. Volba je vždycky jen o směru: pokud podstatné jméno činnost **dělá**, zůstává **-ing**; pokud se činnost **děje jemu**, zůstává **příčestí minulé**.
points: The man who is sitting by the window → the man sitting by the window
The book which was written by her sister → the book written by her sister
It works without be too: the people who live here → the people living here
Only the subject can be reduced this way.

rows: The office was closed, **what** was a problem.
The office was closed, **which** was a problem.
